docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/language.py: GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two FR / EN buttons of
# the navigation bar. Public route: the language must be changeable before
# logging in.
#
# The choice is remembered in a cookie: on each following request, the middleware
# SetLanguage reads it again and sets the language of the request. Then we go back to the page
# we came from (see example 22).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from django.conf import settings
from django.shortcuts import redirect
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET


# code: fr or en (see web/urls.py: /language/de gives a 404 page)
@require_GET
def change(request, code):
    response = redirect(origin_page(request))
    response.set_cookie(settings.LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME, code, max_age=365 * 24 * 3600,
                        secure=settings.COOKIE_SECURE, httponly=True, samesite="Lax")
    return response


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the previous page, from the HTTP "Referer" header sent by the browser. Only
# its path and parameters are kept (/schedule?...): redirecting to a
# full address provided by the request would allow sending the user to
# another site (so-called "open redirect" flaw). urlsplit splits a URL into its
# components: scheme (http), netloc (the machine), path, query...
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def origin_page(request) -> str:
    referer = urlsplit(request.headers.get("Referer", ""))
    path = referer.path
    # "//site.com/..." would be understood by the browser as an address on
    # ANOTHER site: refused too
    if not referer.scheme or not path.startswith("/") or path.startswith("//") \
            or path.startswith("/language/"):
        return "/"
    return f"{path}?{referer.query}" if referer.query else path

The FR / EN buttons on the navigation bar: the language selection is stored in a cookie for one year (example 22), after which the browser returns to the page it came from. The cookie is [HttpOnly]: the [JavaScript] on the page does not need to read it. It is not signed: the [SetLanguage] middleware verifies its value, and an unknown value results in English (see the chapter on scopes).

  • Line 20: [code] is equivalent to [fr] or [en]: the route (a regular expression, [re_path], example 02) accepts only these two values. [/language/de] does not match any route (404 page);
  • lines 34–42: The previous page is specified by the header HTTP [Referer] that the browser sends with the request. This data is provided by the client and is therefore suspect: redirecting to a full URL from the request would allow an attacker to send the user to their own site via a link to [/language/fr] with a fake [Referer] (the so-called “open redirect” vulnerability). Therefore, we retain only the path and parameters ([/schedule?doctorId=1&...]), extracted by the [urlsplit] function from the standard library, which splits a URL into its parts ([scheme], [netloc], [path], [query]...). A path that begins with [//] is also rejected: a browser interprets [//site.com/page] as an address on another site. Finally, you cannot return to [/language/...]: a loop. A backslash ([\]) at the end of a line ([Python]) extends the instruction to the next line.
$ curl -si http://localhost:8081/language/fr -H "Referer: http://localhost:8081/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-30"
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-30
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_language=fr; expires=Mon, 27 Sep 2027 17:56:57 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=31536000; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
...
$ curl -si http://localhost:8081/language/fr -H "Referer: https://pirate.com//page"
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /
...

docs.title: 11.17.4. web/views/auth.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/auth.py: the PUBLIC routes of login:
#   GET  /        redirects to the home page of the role (or to /login)
#   GET  /login   displays the login form (with its captcha)
#   POST /login   checks attempt limit, captcha, login / password
#   POST /logout  logout
#
# Protection against robots, in this order:
#   1. too many recent failures for this login from this IP address?
#      -> immediate refusal, without even looking at the password;
#   2. wrong answer to the captcha? -> refusal (counted as a failure);
#   3. only then, check of the password.
# The password of an attempt refused at steps 1 or 2 is NEVER checked:
# a robot can therefore learn nothing by insisting.
# =========================================================================

from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from models.models import Role
from security import auth, captchas, limiter

from .. import utils


# the home page of each role, just after login: the name of its route
def home_page(role: str) -> str:
    return "area" if role == Role.USER else "schedule"


# GET /: the route is public; the user, if there is one, is known
@require_GET
def home(request):
    if request.user is not None:
        return redirect(home_page(request.user.role))
    return redirect("login")


# GET /login[?login=xxx]: the form; the optional parameter pre-fills the
# login field (used just after the creation of an account, see views/registration.py).
# POST /login: login
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def login(request):
    if request.method == "POST":
        return log_in(request)
    # already logged in (token still valid): straight to the home page
    if request.user is not None:
        return redirect(home_page(request.user.role))
    # [:30]: 30 characters at most
    return page(request, request.GET.get("login", "")[:30], None)


def log_in(request):
    login = request.POST.get("login", "")
    password = request.POST.get("password", "")
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    # 1. too many recent failures? ngettext: the singular or the plural, according to the number
    minutes = limiter.login_block_minutes(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, login, ngettext(
            "Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minute.",
            "Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minutes.",
            minutes) % {"minutes": minutes})
    # 2. the captcha
    if not captchas.verify(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiter.login_failure(ip, login)
        return page(request, login, _("The characters you typed do not match the image. "
                                      "A new image is shown."))
    # 3. the password
    user = auth.validate(login, password) if login and password else None
    if user is None:
        limiter.login_failure(ip, login)
        return page(request, login, _("Incorrect login or password."))
    limiter.login_success(ip, login)
    return auth.set_token(redirect(home_page(user.role)), user)


# POST /logout: clear the token cookie, then go to the login page.
# POST only: a simple link (GET), put on another site, cannot
# log the user out without their knowledge
@require_POST
def logout(request):
    return auth.clear_token(redirect("login"))


# the form, always with a NEW captcha (each image is used only
# once); the entered login is displayed again, never the password. An error: the
# 422 code, as for an invalid form (see example 19)
def page(request, login: str, error: str | None):
    return render(request, "login.html", {
        "page_title": _("Sign in"), "error": error, "login": login,
        "captcha": captchas.generate(),
    }, status=422 if error else 200)

The connection, which follows Example 27:

  • lines 28–29: the home page for each role, along with its route name: “My area” for a patient, and the calendar for others;
  • lines 33–37: the address [/] redirects to the role’s home page or to the login page. The route is public (security/access.py): [request.user] is the user established by the middleware [Authentication], if there is one;
  • lines 43–51: A user who is already logged in is taken directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] of URL pre-fills the field (after an account is created); [[:30]] truncates it to 30 characters;
  • lines 54–76: the login process, in the order shown in Example 27: potential blocking, the CAPTCHA, the password (the anti-CSRF token has already been verified by the middleware). A password is never verified for an attempt rejected by the limiter or the CAPTCHA: a bot learns nothing by persisting. [ngettext(singular, plural, number)] (lines 61–64) selects the appropriate format for the number in the language of the request (Example 22); the parameter [%(minutes)d] is set after translation. If the attempt fails, the page is rendered directly (no redirection): the re-displayed form always has a new CAPTCHA and the entered login. If successful, the login counter is reset to zero, and the browser is redirected to the role’s home page with the token cookie;
  • lines 82–84: Logout deletes the token cookie (Example 25). It only accepts POST, along with the anti-CSRF token: a simple link placed on another site cannot log the user out without their knowledge;
  • lines 90–94: the login page. An error is returned with code 422 (Unprocessable Content), such as an invalid form (example 19).

The login page receives the variable [page_title], the page title, which has already been translated: all views provide this to their template for the [<title>] tag and the page title (see below).

docs.title: 11.17.5. web/views/schedule.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/schedule.py: the schedule page: choice of a doctor and a day,
# schedule of this doctor that day, booking and cancellation of appointments.
#
#   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23              the page
#   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7       the same page, with the
#                                                         booking dialog
#                                                         of slot 7 open
#   POST /schedule/book                                   creates an appointment
#   POST /schedule/cancel                                 cancels an appointment
#
# The whole page is described by its URL: it can be reloaded, bookmarked,
# the "Back" button of the browser can be used - without a single line of
# JavaScript.
#
# What each one sees and can do:
#
#   | role          | taken slot displayed              | Book               | Cancel  |
#   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
#   | ADMIN, DOCTOR | name of the patient               | for a patient      | yes     |
#   |               |                                   | chosen in a list   |         |
#   | USER (patient)| "Booked", or THEIR name if it is  | for themselves, if | no (*)  |
#   |               | their own appointment             | they have no       |         |
#   |               |                                   | upcoming appt.     |         |
#
#   (*) the patient cancels their appointment from their "My area" page.
#
# CONFIDENTIALITY: for a patient, the name of the OTHER patients is not
# simply hidden by the template - it is never passed to the template. The HTML
# sent to the browser therefore does not contain it, even hidden (a simple "View
# page source" would reveal it otherwise).
#
# No booking in the past: the "Book" button only appears for
# today and the following days (and the business layer would refuse it
# anyway).
#
# Security: all the /schedule URLs require an authenticated user, and
# /schedule/cancel the ADMIN or DOCTOR role (see security/access.py).
# =========================================================================

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.core.exceptions import BadRequest
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_POST

from domain.schedule import DoctorDaySchedule
from business import errors
from business.dates import today
from business.errors import BusinessError
from models.models import Client, Person, Role

from .. import utils
from ..application import application
from ..view_models import BookingView, OptionView, ScheduleRow, ScheduleView


# who is logged in, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rights:
    manager: bool                      # ADMIN or DOCTOR
    patient: Client | None             # the logged-in client (USER role), otherwise None
    patient_can_book: bool             # a USER without an upcoming appointment


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /schedule
# The URL parameters are read raw (request.GET), to distinguish a
# MISSING parameter (None) from an EMPTY parameter (?doctorId=).
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def show(request):
    error = None
    user = utils.user(request)
    rights = compute_rights(request)
    app = application()
    # the day: that of the URL if it is valid, otherwise today
    day = today()
    raw_day = request.GET.get("day")
    if raw_day is not None:
        requested_day = utils.valid_date(raw_day)
        if requested_day is not None:
            day = requested_day
        else:
            error = _("The requested date is not valid.")
    bookable_day = day >= today()
    # the doctor: that of the URL; failing that, for a logged-in doctor, themselves
    raw_doctor_id = request.GET.get("doctorId")
    doctor_id = utils.positive_integer(raw_doctor_id)
    if raw_doctor_id is None and user.role == Role.DOCTOR:
        doctor = app.get_doctor_by_user_id(user.user_id)
        doctor_id = doctor.id if doctor else None
    # the drop-down list of the doctors
    doctors = [option(d, d.id == doctor_id) for d in app.get_all_doctors()]
    # the schedule, if a doctor is chosen (and the date valid)
    schedule = None
    if doctor_id is not None and error is None:
        doctor_schedule = app.get_doctor_day_schedule(doctor_id, day)
        if doctor_schedule is None:
            error = _("This doctor does not exist (any more).")
        else:
            schedule = schedule_view(doctor_schedule, rights, bookable_day)
    # the booking dialog: only if the requested slot can be booked by
    # this user
    booking = None
    slot_id = utils.positive_integer(request.GET.get("book"))
    if schedule is not None and slot_id is not None:
        row = next((r for r in schedule.rows if r.slot_id == slot_id and r.bookable), None)
        if row is not None:
            booking = BookingView(
                row.slot_id,
                row.time_range,
                [option(c, False) for c in app.get_all_clients()] if rights.manager else [],
                rights.patient.label() if rights.patient else None)
    return render(request, "schedule.html", {
        "page_title": _("Schedule"),
        "error": error,
        "doctors": doctors,
        "doctor_id": doctor_id,
        "day": utils.iso(day),
        "schedule": schedule,
        "booking": booking,
        # the displayed schedule, without booking dialog
        "back_url": schedule_url(doctor_id, day) if doctor_id is not None else reverse("schedule"),
        "info": patient_info(rights, schedule),
    })


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /schedule/book   fields: doctorId, day, slotId, clientId
#
# For a patient (USER), the clientId field is IGNORED: they always book for
# themselves. Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a
# clever patient to book in the name of another one.
#
# "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern: whatever the result, no page is built
# here - a flash message is left and we redirect to the schedule (see example 20).
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def book(request):
    doctor_id, day = requested_schedule(request)
    slot_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("slotId"))
    if doctor_id is None or slot_id is None:
        # -> "invalid request" page (see web/middleware.py)
        raise BadRequest("invalid schedule or slot")
    app = application()
    user = utils.user(request)
    if user.is_patient:
        client = utils.connected_patient(request)
    else:
        client_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("clientId"))
        if client_id is None:
            # no patient chosen: the booking dialog is opened again
            messages.error(request, _("Choose a patient."))
            return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day, slot_id))
        client = app.get_client_by_id(client_id)
    slot = app.get_slot_by_id(slot_id)
    if client is None:
        messages.error(request, _("This patient does not exist (any more)."))
    elif slot is None or slot.doctor_id != doctor_id:
        messages.error(request, _("This slot does not exist (any more)."))
    else:
        try:
            # the rules (not in the past, a single upcoming appointment per
            # patient, free slot) are checked by the business layer
            app.add_appointment(day, slot, client)
            messages.success(request, _("Appointment booked."))
        except BusinessError as e:
            # same rule, but a message in the 2nd person when it is the patient
            # themselves who books ("You already have..." rather than "This patient...").
            # The other exceptions (real anomalies) are not caught: 500 page
            if e.code == errors.PATIENT_HAS_APPOINTMENT and user.is_patient:
                messages.error(request, _("You already have an upcoming appointment: "
                                          "cancel it to book another one."))
            else:
                messages.error(request, e.message)
    return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /schedule/cancel   fields: appointmentId, doctorId, day
# (a patient cancels THEIR appointment from "My area", not from here)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def cancel(request):
    doctor_id, day = requested_schedule(request)
    appointment_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("appointmentId"))
    if doctor_id is None or appointment_id is None:
        raise BadRequest("invalid schedule or appointment")
    app = application()
    appointment = app.get_appointment_by_id(appointment_id)
    if appointment is None:
        # already cancelled (by someone else, or double click)
        messages.error(request, _("This appointment does not exist (any more)."))
    else:
        app.delete_appointment(appointment)
        messages.success(request, _("Appointment cancelled."))
    return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# who is logged in, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def compute_rights(request) -> Rights:
    if not utils.user(request).is_patient:
        return Rights(manager=True, patient=None, patient_can_book=False)
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    upcoming = application().get_client_upcoming_appointments(patient.id)
    # not list: true for an empty list
    return Rights(manager=False, patient=patient, patient_can_book=not upcoming)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the schedule of the doctor, formatted for the template - and filtered according to the rights
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def schedule_view(doctor_schedule: DoctorDaySchedule, rights: Rights, bookable_day: bool) -> ScheduleView:
    doctor_id = doctor_schedule.doctor.id
    day = doctor_schedule.day
    rows = []
    for dds in doctor_schedule.doctor_day_slots:
        slot = dds.slot
        appointment = dds.appointment
        free = appointment is None
        # the appointment of the logged-in patient?
        me = appointment is not None and rights.patient is not None and appointment.client_id == rights.patient.id
        rows.append(ScheduleRow(
            slot_id=slot.id,
            time_range=slot.time_range(),
            free=free,
            # THE confidentiality point: a patient only receives the name of THEIR
            # appointment; for the others, None (the template displays "Booked")
            patient=appointment.client.label() if appointment is not None and (rights.manager or me) else None,
            me=me,
            bookable=free and bookable_day and (rights.manager or rights.patient_can_book),
            book_url=schedule_url(doctor_id, day, slot.id),
            appointment_id=appointment.id if appointment is not None and rights.manager else None))
    return ScheduleView(doctor_schedule.doctor.label(), utils.format_day(day), rows)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions
# the hidden fields doctorId / day of the POST forms; (None, None) if they are
# invalid
def requested_schedule(request) -> tuple[int | None, date | None]:
    doctor_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("doctorId"))
    day = utils.valid_date(request.POST.get("day"))
    return (None, None) if doctor_id is None or day is None else (doctor_id, day)


# /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23[&book=7]: reverse builds the path of the
# route, urlencode the URL parameters, correctly encoded (see example 04)
def schedule_url(doctor_id: int, day: date, book: int | None = None) -> str:
    parameters = {"doctorId": doctor_id, "day": utils.iso(day)}
    if book is not None:
        parameters["book"] = book
    return f"{reverse('schedule')}?{urlencode(parameters)}"


def option(p: Person, selected: bool) -> OptionView:
    return OptionView(p.id, p.label(), selected)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the information message of a patient who already has an upcoming appointment (why
# there is no "Book" button), or None. Useless if THEIR appointment appears
# in the displayed schedule (in blue): this is the case just after they have
# booked it, where the message would be out of place
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
def patient_info(rights: Rights, schedule: ScheduleView | None) -> str | None:
    if rights.patient is None or rights.patient_can_book:
        return None
    appointment_shown = schedule is not None and any(r.me for r in schedule.rows)
    return None if appointment_shown else _("You already have an upcoming appointment: "
                                            "cancel it to book another one.")

The application’s main page. The header comment summarizes what each user sees and can do.

docs.title: 11.17.5.1. The URL elements of the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-30] displays Doctor 1’s schedule for that day; [&book=4] also opens the window for booking Slot 4. You can reload the page, bookmark it, or use the browser’s Back button without a single line of [JavaScript]. The form at the top of the page (for selecting the doctor and the day) is a GET form (example 17): it reloads the page with new parameters. The appointment booking window is opened by a simple link and closed by a link to the same page without the [book] parameter.

docs.title: 11.17.5.2. GET /schedule
docs.text:
Lines 76–131:

  • the parameters for URL are read as raw data ([request.GET.get("day")]), without a form: a missing parameter ([None]) is not an error (it defaults to today or no doctor); an invalid date is an error, displayed at the bottom of the page (the doctor and day selections remain displayed, but not the calendar); a doctor or time slot number that is not a positive integer is simply ignored;
  • A logged-in user who has not selected a doctor sees their own schedule: the system searches for their doctor based on their account ([get_doctor_by_user_id]);
  • the drop-down list of doctors: a parsed list converts each doctor's name to [OptionView];
  • the calendar, formatted and filtered according to the user’s permissions ([schedule_view], below);
  • the booking window, only if the requested time slot is bookable by that user: a patient who attempts to generate the URL [&book=2] for a booked time slot would get nothing. [next(...)] returns the first line of the appropriate calendar, or [None]. The list of patients is provided only to the administrator and doctors; a patient sees only their own name;
  • the template receives its variables ([render], example 13), including [page_title] and [error], which are read by the base template.

docs.title: 11.17.5.3. POST /schedule/book
docs.text:
Lines 144–182:

  • the hidden fields of the appointment form (doctor, day, time slot). Invalid; this can only be a manually created request: [BadRequest], the “invalid request” page (400), via the middleware [ErrorPage];
  • For a patient, the field [clientId] is ignored: the patient always books for themselves ([utils.connected_patient]). Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name. For the administrator and doctors, a patient must have been selected; otherwise, the reservation window reopens with a message;
  • the time slot must belong to the doctor on the page ([slot.doctor_id]: the foreign key, without a query);
  • the business rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer. A [BusinessError] becomes a flash error message. The same rejection, “one upcoming appointment,” is displayed to the second person on behalf of the patient themselves (“You already have…”). Any other exception is not intercepted: this is a true error (500 page);
  • in all cases, the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (example 20) applies: a pop-up message and a redirect to the calendar.

docs.title: 11.17.5.4. POST /schedule/cancel
docs.text: Lines 189–203: Cancellation of an appointment by the administrator or a doctor (rule [^/schedule/cancel$] derived from [security/access.py]). An appointment that no longer exists (already canceled by someone else, or due to a double-click) is not an error: it’s just a message.

docs.title: 11.17.5.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions
docs.text:
• lines 64–68 and 209–215: what the user is authorized to do on the page, within a data class: is the user an administrator (ADMIN or DOCTOR)? a patient (and which one)? Can this patient make a reservation (no upcoming appointments)? [not list] is true for an empty list;
  • Lines 221–242: the doctor’s schedule, converted into rows for the template. The confidentiality issue is on line 237: a patient is shown only the name of their appointment. For the others, the attribute [patient] is set to [None], and the template displays “Booked.” The name is not masked by the template: it is never transmitted to the template and therefore does not appear in the page’s source code, where it would be easy to read. The “Book” button is displayed for an available time slot on a future date to an administrator or a patient who can make a reservation; the “Cancel” button is displayed only to administrators. The named parameters ([slot_id=slot.id]) make the construction of an object with eight attributes readable;
  • lines 248–251: the hidden fields of the POST forms. The function returns a tuple, which the view unpacks into two variables ([doctor_id, day = requested_schedule(request)], lines 146 and 191);
  • lines 256–260: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day. [reverse("schedule")] returns the route path; [urlencode] generates the parameters, correctly encoded: [/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-30];
  • lines 273–278: the message explaining to a patient why there is no “Book” button (they already have an upcoming appointment), unless that appointment is in the displayed calendar (immediately after booking it, the message would be moved). [any(...)]: Does at least one line check the condition?

docs.title: 11.17.6. web/views/persons.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/persons.py: the management of doctors and that of clients (reserved to
# the ADMIN) are IDENTICAL: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
# writing the same views twice, they are written once, as the METHODS
# of a class, PersonManagement; two OBJECTS of this class, doctors and
# clients, only differ by what distinguishes them: the name of the section
# (doctors or clients), the texts, and the methods of the ApplicationModel to call.
#
# A method of an object is called with the object (self): the view object.list(request)
# thus knows which section it is about. The urls() method builds the routes of
# the section:
#
#   GET  /doctors                    list                      doctors_list
#   GET  /doctors/add                empty form                doctors_add
#   POST /doctors/add                creation                  doctors_add
#   GET  /doctors/{id}/edit          pre-filled form           doctors_edit
#   POST /doctors/{id}/edit          update                    doctors_edit
#   POST /doctors/{id}/delete        deletion                  doctors_delete
#
# (and the same URLs under /clients). The templates are common too:
# templates/persons/list.html and persons/form.html.
#
# SECURITY: the rule ^/(doctors|clients) of security/access.py reserves all these
# URLs to the ADMIN - including those that would be added later.
# =========================================================================

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from django.contrib import messages
from django.http import Http404
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import path, reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from business import errors
from business.errors import BusinessError
from models.models import Person

from ..application import application
from ..forms import PersonForm

# the form fields concerned by each "input" business error (a
# duplicate): they are framed in red, the message being at the bottom of the page
BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS = {
    errors.LOGIN_TAKEN: ["login"],
    errors.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS: ["first_name", "last_name"],
    errors.CLIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS: ["first_name", "last_name"],
}


# the texts specific to each type of person; %(name)s, %(login)s: the
# parameters of the messages
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Texts:
    title: str                  # "Doctors"
    add: str                    # "Add a doctor"
    edit: str                   # "Edit a doctor"
    empty: str                  # "No doctors."
    confirm_delete: str         # "Delete this doctor... ?"
    added: str                  # "Doctor %(name)s has been added (login: %(login)s)."
    updated: str
    deleted: str


class PersonManagement:
    def __init__(self, section: str, texts: Texts, list_all: Callable, find: Callable,
                 create: Callable, update: Callable, remove: Callable):
        # "doctors" or "clients": the start of the path and of the name of the routes
        self.section = section
        self.texts = texts
        # the methods of the ApplicationModel to call (functions, see below)
        self.list_all = list_all
        self.find = find
        self.create = create
        self.update = update
        self.remove = remove

    # the routes of the section; self.list: the method bound to THIS object
    def urls(self):
        s = self.section
        return [
            path(f"{s}", require_GET(self.list), name=f"{s}_list"),
            path(f"{s}/add", require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])(self.add), name=f"{s}_add"),
            path(f"{s}/<int:id>/edit", require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])(self.edit),
                 name=f"{s}_edit"),
            path(f"{s}/<int:id>/delete", require_POST(self.delete), name=f"{s}_delete"),
        ]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors (or /clients)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def list(self, request):
        return render(request, "persons/list.html", {
            "page_title": self.texts.title, "texts": self.texts, "section": self.section,
            "add_url": reverse(f"{self.section}_add"), "persons": self.list_all()})

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors/add: the empty form; POST: the creation
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def add(self, request):
        if request.method == "GET":
            return self.page(request, PersonForm(initial={"title": "Mr"}), None)
        form = PersonForm(request.POST)
        if not form.is_valid():
            return self.page(request, form, None)
        try:
            person = self.create(form.person_data())
        except BusinessError as e:
            return self.business_error(request, e, form, None)
        messages.success(request, str(self.texts.added) % parameters(person))
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_list")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors/{id}/edit: the pre-filled form; POST: the update.
    # <int:id>: a parameter made of digits (see example 02):
    # /doctors/abc/edit matches no route (404 page)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def edit(self, request, id):
        person = self.find(id)
        if person is None:
            raise Http404("unknown person")
        if request.method == "GET":
            # the form, pre-filled with the values of the person (the
            # password itself is never displayed)
            form = PersonForm(creation=False, initial={
                "title": person.title, "first_name": person.first_name, "last_name": person.last_name,
                "login": person.account.login, "version": person.version})
            return self.page(request, form, person)
        form = PersonForm(request.POST, creation=False)
        if not form.is_valid():
            return self.page(request, form, person)
        try:
            person = self.update(id, form.person_data())
        except BusinessError as e:
            return self.business_error(request, e, form, person)
        messages.success(request, str(self.texts.updated) % parameters(person))
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_list")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # POST /doctors/{id}/delete (the "Are you sure?" confirmation is requested
    # before the form is sent, see static/js/app.js)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def delete(self, request, id):
        person = self.find(id)
        try:
            self.remove(id)
            messages.success(request, str(self.texts.deleted) % parameters(person))
        except BusinessError as e:
            messages.error(request, e.message)
        return redirect(f"{self.section}_list")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
    # person None: creation form; otherwise: update form.
    # A refused form (invalid input, or business rule): the 422 code
    def page(self, request, form, person, error=None, invalid_fields=()):
        refused = error is not None or (form.is_bound and bool(form.errors))
        title = self.texts.add if person is None else self.texts.edit
        return render(request, "persons/form.html", {
            "page_title": title,
            "form": form.flag(invalid_fields),
            "error": error,
            "list_url": reverse(f"{self.section}_list"),
        }, status=422 if refused else 200)

    # a business rule has refused the write: the form is displayed again, with
    # the input of the user (without the password), the message of the business
    # layer (at the bottom of the page), and the fields concerned, if any, framed in
    # red so that the user immediately sees what to correct
    def business_error(self, request, e: BusinessError, form, person):
        if e.code in (errors.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND, errors.CLIENT_NOT_FOUND):
            # deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: back to the list
            messages.error(request, e.message)
            return redirect(f"{self.section}_list")
        return self.page(request, form, person, e.message, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.code, []))


# the %(name)s and %(login)s parameters of the "added / updated / deleted" messages
def parameters(person: Person | None) -> dict:
    if person is None:
        return {"name": "", "login": ""}
    return {"name": f"{person.first_name} {person.last_name}", "login": person.account.login}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the two objects. lambda: a small anonymous function, which calls the right
# method of the ApplicationModel at the time of the request. The texts are translated
# "lazily" (gettext_lazy): at the time they are displayed, in the
# language of the request, and not when the module is loaded
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

doctors = PersonManagement(
    "doctors",
    Texts(_("Doctors"), _("Add a doctor"), _("Edit a doctor"), _("No doctors."),
          _("Delete this doctor, their time slots and their user account?"),
          _("Doctor %(name)s has been added (login: %(login)s)."),
          _("Doctor %(name)s has been updated."), _("Doctor %(name)s has been deleted.")),
    list_all=lambda: application().get_all_doctors(),
    find=lambda id: application().get_doctor_by_id(id),
    create=lambda data: application().add_doctor(data),
    update=lambda id, data: application().edit_doctor(id, data),
    remove=lambda id: application().delete_doctor(id))

clients = PersonManagement(
    "clients",
    Texts(_("Patients"), _("Add a patient"), _("Edit a patient"), _("No patients."),
          _("Delete this patient, their user account and all their appointments?"),
          _("Patient %(name)s has been added (login: %(login)s)."),
          _("Patient %(name)s has been updated."), _("Patient %(name)s has been deleted.")),
    list_all=lambda: application().get_all_clients(),
    find=lambda id: application().get_client_by_id(id),
    create=lambda data: application().add_client(data),
    update=lambda id, data: application().edit_client(id, data),
    remove=lambda id: application().delete_client(id))

The management of doctors and clients is identical: same list, same form, same rules. The views are written once, like the methods of a class, [PersonManagement]; two objects of this class, [doctors] and [clients], differ only in what sets them apart: the section name, the text, and the methods of [ApplicationModel] to be called. A view does not have to be a function: it is any callable object that receives a request and returns a response. [self.list], a method associated with an object, is one such view: [Django] calls it with the request, and the method also receives its object ([self]), which is its section. To add a view to the doctor management and client management sections, simply write it here.

  • Lines 46–50: the fields affected by each business-logic data entry error: a duplicate username affects the “login” field; a name conflict affects the “first name” and “last name” fields. These fields will be highlighted in red;
  • Lines 55–64: The texts specific to each section, in a data class;
  • lines 68–78: the constructor. The last five parameters are functions ([Callable]): read the list, find, create, modify, or delete a person;
  • lines 81–89: the routes of the section. Decorators are called here as functions ([require_GET(self.list)]: the decorated view [self.list]): this is exactly what the syntax [@require_GET] does when placed above a function (Example 02). The prefix for the path and the route names is the section: the view [list] becomes the routes [doctors_list] ([/doctors]) and [clients_list] ([/clients]);
  • lines 94–97: the list. The template is shared by both sections: it receives the text from the section and the URL from the add button;
  • lines 102–113: the add function. A single view for GET (the empty form, with the title [Mr] selected via [initial], Example 18) and POST (creation), as shown in Example 19. An invalid entry re-displays the form. A valid entry proceeds to the business layer, which may reject the write operation (due to a homonym or a login already in use); otherwise, a success message flashes and the user returns to the list (schema PRG). The message text is a lazy translation: [str(...)] translates it before the [%] operator inserts its parameters;
  • lines 120–139: the update, for a person who exists; otherwise, [Http404] returns a 404 page. [<int:id>] accepts only numbers for the [id] parameter (e.g., 02) and converts it to an integer. The GET form is pre-filled with the person’s values and their version; a POST form receives the input;
  • lines 145–152: deletion. The form requested confirmation in the browser (example 21). The person is retrieved before deletion for the success message (“Doctor Paul TATOU has been deleted.”);
  • lines 157–165: the form, for creation ([person] equals [None]) or modification. A rejected form (invalid input or business rule violation) is returned with status code 422 (example 19). Here, [flag] highlights the fields with errors in red;
  • lines 171–176: the business layer rejected the write operation. If a person has been deleted in the meantime (by another administrator): return to the list. Otherwise, the form is redisplayed directly (without redirection), as with an input error: it already contains the user’s input. Added to this are the business layer message (displayed at the bottom of the page, in the error area) and the fields to be highlighted in red;
  • lines 180–183: the parameters [%(name)s] and [%(login)s] for success messages;
  • lines 193–215: the two objects. Each [lambda] calls the appropriate method of [ApplicationModel] when the request is made: the facade is not created when the module loads, but when it is first used.

docs.title: 11.17.7. web/views/registration.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/registration.py: "Create a patient account": a patient who does not
# have an account yet creates it themselves. PUBLIC routes (one has no account yet,
# by definition):
#
#   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the
#                             authentication page: checks the captcha of THIS
#                             page, then opens the form
#   GET  /register            the form
#   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
#
# The path is protected against robots by ONE captcha, that of the
# authentication page:
#   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form to
#      /register/access; if the captcha is typed correctly, the server issues a
#      pass (see security/registration_pass.py);
#   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the
#      authentication page (decorator @registration_pass_required);
#   3. the pass is consumed on creation: a solved captcha allows the creation of
#      ONE account;
#   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is limited
#      (see security/limiter.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the "Patients" page
# (same method of the business layer: add_client), except that the patient
# CHOOSES their login and password (required, with confirmation).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods, require_POST

from business.errors import BusinessError
from security import captchas, limiter, registration_pass
from security.registration_pass import registration_pass_required

from .. import utils
from ..application import application
from ..forms import RegistrationForm
from .persons import BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS


# the "too many accounts created" message, in the singular or in the plural
def too_many_accounts(minutes: int) -> str:
    return ngettext(
        "Too many accounts have been created from your connection. Try again in %(minutes)d minute.",
        "Too many accounts have been created from your connection. Try again in %(minutes)d minutes.",
        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /register/access   fields: captcha_id, captcha (those of the
# authentication page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def access(request):
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    # too many accounts created recently from this address: no point going further
    minutes = limiter.registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        messages.error(request, too_many_accounts(minutes))
        return redirect("login")
    # missing or wrong captcha: back to the authentication page, with a
    # new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
    if not captchas.verify(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiter.login_failure(ip, "")
        messages.error(request, _("To create an account, first type the characters shown in the image "
                                  "correctly, then click \"Create a patient account\"."))
        return redirect("login")
    # correct captcha: the pass is issued and the form is opened
    return registration_pass.issue(redirect("registration"))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /register: the form; POST /register: the creation. The
# pass has been checked BEFORE the call of the view (@registration_pass_required).
# The form validates ALL the input (fields and password confirmation):
# the user corrects all their errors in one go
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
@registration_pass_required
def registration(request):
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, RegistrationForm(initial={"title": "Mr"}))
    form = RegistrationForm(request.POST)
    if not form.is_valid():
        return page(request, form)
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    # 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiter.registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, form, too_many_accounts(minutes))
    # 2. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
    data = form.person_data()
    try:
        application().add_client(data)
    except BusinessError as e:
        # login or first + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return page(request, form, e.message, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.code, []))
    # 3. the pass has been used: it will not allow the creation of a 2nd account
    registration_pass.consume(request.COOKIES.get(registration_pass.COOKIE))
    limiter.registration_success(ip)
    # 4. back to the login page, login pre-filled
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been created. You can now log in with "
                                "the login %(login)s.") % {"login": data.login})
    url = f"{reverse('login')}?{urlencode({'login': data.login})}"
    return registration_pass.clear_cookie(redirect(url))


# the form; a refused form: the 422 code
def page(request, form, error=None, invalid_fields=()):
    refused = error is not None or (form.is_bound and bool(form.errors))
    return render(request, "registration.html", {
        "page_title": _("Create a patient account"),
        "form": form.flag(invalid_fields), "error": error,
    }, status=422 if refused else 200)

The patient creates a patient account themselves. The flow is protected by a CAPTCHA, the same one used on the login page.

  • Lines 59–75: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page submits the login form to this address (which later becomes the template [login.html]). If too many accounts have been created recently from this address (IP), there is no need to proceed further. If the CAPTCHA is missing or incorrect: return to the login page with a new image and a message; the failure counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username). If the CAPTCHA is correct: a token is stored in a cookie, and the user is redirected to the form;
  • lines 84–91: the form. The [@registration_pass_required] decorator (line 85) checks the token before calling the view. The order of the decorators matters: the one closest to the function is applied first; [require_http_methods], placed above, therefore rejects a prohibited method before any other checks. The form validates the entire input, including password confirmation: the user sees all their errors at once;
  • Lines 92–111: account creation. The client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator ([add_client]); only the username and password are chosen by the patient. If a username or a homonym is already taken: return to the form without consuming the token. Creating an account consumes the token (one solved CAPTCHA equals one account), counts toward the hourly limit, and redirects to the login page with the username pre-filled (parameter [?login=...], generated by [urlencode]), along with a success message. The pass cookie is cleared.

docs.title: 11.17.8. web/views/area.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/views/area.py: the PERSONAL pages of the patient (USER role), the one they
# see just after logging in:
#
#   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account], [View a
#                                  schedule], and their upcoming appointment
#   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
#   GET  /my-account               update form of their account
#   POST /my-account               update
#   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
#
# Golden rule of this module: the patient concerned is ALWAYS the one of the token
# (utils.connected_patient), never an identifier sent by the browser. A
# patient can therefore neither see, nor modify, nor cancel what belongs to another
# patient, even by building their requests themselves.
#
# Any update or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT password:
# someone who found a session left open could neither change the
# password, nor delete the account. The current password errors are
# counted as login failures (same limit).
#
# Security: all these URLs are reserved to the USER role (rule ^/my- of
# security/access.py).
# =========================================================================

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from business.errors import BusinessError
from models.models import Client
from security import auth, limiter

from .. import utils
from ..application import application
from ..forms import MyAccountForm
from ..view_models import AppointmentView
from .schedule import schedule_url
from .persons import BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-area
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def area(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    appointments = [AppointmentView(
        a.id,
        utils.format_day(a.day),
        a.slot.time_range(),
        a.slot.doctor.label(),
        # link to the schedule of the doctor that day: the patient sees their name there
        schedule_url(a.slot.doctor_id, a.day))
        for a in application().get_client_upcoming_appointments(patient.id)]
    return render(request, "area.html", {"page_title": _("My area"),
                                         "patient": patient.label(), "appointments": appointments})


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def cancel_appointment(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    appointment_id = utils.positive_integer(request.POST.get("appointmentId"))
    appointment = application().get_appointment_by_id(appointment_id) if appointment_id is not None else None
    # an appointment that does not exist, and that of ANOTHER patient, get the same
    # answer: nothing is revealed about the appointments of the others
    if appointment is None or appointment.client_id != patient.id:
        messages.error(request, _("This appointment does not exist (any more)."))
    else:
        application().delete_appointment(appointment)
        messages.success(request, _("Appointment cancelled."))
    return redirect("area")


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account: the form, pre-filled with the values of the patient;
# POST /my-account: the update
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def account(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, MyAccountForm(initial={
            "title": patient.title, "first_name": patient.first_name, "last_name": patient.last_name,
            "login": patient.account.login, "version": patient.version}))
    form = MyAccountForm(request.POST)
    if not form.is_valid():
        return page(request, form)
    # the current password; wrong: the message goes UNDER the field (an error added
    # to the field by add_error), and at the bottom of the page
    error = check_current_password(request, patient, form.cleaned_data["current_password"])
    if error is not None:
        form.add_error("current_password", error)
        return page(request, form, error)
    try:
        client = application().edit_client(patient.id, form.person_data())
    except BusinessError as e:
        return page(request, form, e.message, BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.code, []))
    # the login and the displayed name are IN the token: a new one is issued, otherwise
    # the navigation bar would keep the old name
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been updated."))
    return auth.set_token(redirect("area"), client.account)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete   field: current_password
# The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together, then the
# patient is logged out.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def delete_account(request):
    patient = utils.connected_patient(request)
    error = check_current_password(request, patient, request.POST.get("current_password", ""))
    if error is not None:
        messages.error(request, error)
        return redirect("account")
    application().delete_client(patient.id)
    messages.success(request, _("Your account has been deleted."))
    return auth.clear_token(redirect("login"))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
# the account page; a refused form: the 422 code
def page(request, form, error=None, invalid_fields=()):
    refused = error is not None or (form.is_bound and bool(form.errors))
    return render(request, "account.html", {
        "page_title": _("Manage my account"),
        "form": form.flag(invalid_fields), "error": error,
    }, status=422 if refused else 200)


# None if the current password is correct; otherwise the error message
def check_current_password(request, patient: Client, password: str) -> str | None:
    ip = utils.ip(request)
    login = patient.account.login
    minutes = limiter.login_block_minutes(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return ngettext("Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minute.",
                        "Too many failed attempts. Try again in %(minutes)d minutes.",
                        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}
    if not password or auth.validate(login, password) is None:
        limiter.login_failure(ip, login)
        return _("Incorrect current password.")
    return None

The patient’s personal pages. The golden rule of this module: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token ([utils.connected_patient]), never an identifier sent by the browser. A patient cannot therefore view, modify, or cancel information belonging to another patient, even if they generate their own requests.

  • Lines 46–58: My area: the patient’s name and their upcoming appointments, formatted ([AppointmentView]), each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The function [schedule_url] is part of the calendar module (line 39, [from .schedule import schedule_url]);
  • lines 64–76: the cancellation of his appointment. Both a nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments (not even their existence);
  • lines 83–92: the “Manage my account” form, pre-filled with the patient’s information, and its submission;
  • lines 95–106: the modification. Any modification requires the current password: someone who found a session left open would be unable to change the password or do anything else. If the current password is incorrect, the form is redisplayed, with the message below the field and at the bottom of the page. [add_error(field, message)] adds an error to a field, as if validation had detected it (example 19). After the modification, a new token is generated: the login and the displayed name are included in the token, and the navigation bar would otherwise retain the old name until the next login;
  • lines 114–123: deletion of the account, the client, and all their appointments, using the same business-logic method as for the administrator. This second form on the page is hand-coded (a single field: the current password). The patient is then logged out (the token cookie is cleared);
  • lines 137–148: Verification of the current password. This is subject to the attempt limiter, just like a login: without this, someone with an open session could try thousands of passwords via the “Manage my account” form and discover the correct one.

docs.title: 11.18. The Templates
docs.text: The templates in the [templates] folder (configuration [TEMPLATES] derived from [config/settings.py]): a parent template, fragments, named form fragments, and pages.

docs.title: 11.18.1.1. templates/layout.html
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/layout.html
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The PARENT template of all the pages (see example 15): each page
  (schedule.html, login.html...) EXTENDS it ({% extends %}) and fills its
  [content] block.

  Django ESCAPES everything it displays with {{ ... }} (the characters < > & " '
  become < >...): protection against HTML injection through an entered
  name, for example. To insert HTML as is, it must be requested
  explicitly (safe filter, see fragments/captcha.html).

  Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page, an error at the BOTTOM, on a light
  pink background (success_zone and error_zone tags, see web/templatetags/rdv.py).

  The template shares the variables of the page: [page_title] (the title of the
  page, passed on by the view, already translated). LANGUAGE_CODE: the language of the
  request (see web/middleware.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load static i18n rdv %}
<html lang="{{ LANGUAGE_CODE }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{ page_title }} - RdvMedecins</title>
  {# static: the URL of a file of the static folder #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css' %}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/styles.css' %}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% success_zone %}
    <main>
      {% block content %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% error_zone %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden as long as it is not needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{% static 'js/app.js' %}"></script>
</body>
</html>

The parent template for all pages (Example 15): each page extends it ([{% extends "layout.html" %}]) and fills in its [content] block (line 38).

  • Line 23: the tag libraries used: [static] (static files), [i18n] (translations, Example 22), and [rdv], ours (web layer, above). A parent template does not pass its libraries on to the templates that extend it: each page loads the ones it needs;
  • line 24: the page’s language, [fr] or [en]: the active language of the request, set by the [SetLanguage] middleware;
  • line 28: the page title, already translated by the view, which passes it in the variable [page_title];
  • lines 30–31: the [{% static %}] tag renders the URL from a file in the [static] folder (Example 15);
  • lines 35–40: the navigation bar, the success messages at the top of the page, the page content, and the error area at the bottom of the page. The navigation bar snippet is inserted by [{% include %}] (Example 15): it accesses the page’s variables. The two message areas are the inclusion tags from [web/templatetags/rdv.py];
  • lines 43–44: the “Are you sure?” window, hidden until needed, and the script that displays it.

The header comment (lines 2–22) is a [{% comment %}] tag: a template comment that can span multiple lines ([{# ... #}] fits on a single line, example 14). It is written after [<!doctype html>]: the first line of the sent page must be the document type declaration. The DTL escapes everything it displays using [{{ ... }}] (Example 14): a user-entered name containing HTML ([<script>]) is displayed as-is, without being interpreted. This prevents HTML (XSS) from being injected effortlessly into all pages.

docs.title: 11.18.1.2. templates/fragments/navbar.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/navbar.html - the navigation bar.

  Title, FR/EN, role, name, logout - and the menu, whose entries depend
  on the role: they are computed by the context processor web/contexts.py
  (variable menu), with, for each one, its URL, its label, and whether it is the one
  of the current page ("active" class).

  user: the logged-in user, or None (see web/contexts.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">RdvMedecins</span>

  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% for entry in menu %}
    <li class="nav-item">
      <a class="nav-link{% if entry.active %} active{% endif %}" href="{{ entry.url }}">{{ entry.label }}</a>
    </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted #}
    {% get_available_languages as languages %}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code, name in languages %}
      <a class="btn {% if code == LANGUAGE_CODE %}btn-light{% else %}btn-outline-light{% endif %}"
         href="{% url 'language' code %}">{{ code|upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if user %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ user.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ user.name }}</span>
    {# logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and to the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}" class="m-0">
      {% csrf_token %}
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{% translate "Log out" %}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>

The navigation bar. It simply displays what the [web/contexts.py] context processor has prepared: the logged-in user ([user]), and the menu items ([menu]), which depend on the role.

  • lines 17–23: the menu, with each entry having its own URL and label; the [active] class of [Bootstrap] highlights the entry for the currently displayed page;
  • Lines 27–32: the FR / EN buttons, simple links ([/language/fr]), with the active language highlighted. [{% get_available_languages as languages %}] (library [i18n]) stores the setting [LANGUAGES]—a list of (code, name) pairs—in the variable [languages], which the loop unpacks ([{% for code, name in languages %}]); the filter [upper] capitalizes the code. [{% url 'language' code %}] creates URL for a route that has a parameter (example 15);
  • Lines 35–43: For a logged-in user, their role, name, and the logout button. Logout is a request for POST: a form reduced to just its button, with its anti-CSRF token ([{% csrf_token %}], Example 21).

docs.title: 11.18.1.3. templates/fragments/success.html and errors.html
docs.text:
{# templates/fragments/success.html - the SUCCESS messages (success_zone tag, see web/templatetags/rdv.py) #}
{% for text in texts %}
<div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ text }}</div>
{% endfor %}

{% comment %}
  templates/fragments/errors.html - the error zone, at the BOTTOM of each page, on a
  light pink background (class .error-zone, see static/css/styles.css). The messages
  are gathered by the error_zone tag (see web/templatetags/rdv.py).
  role="alert": a screen reader announces the message as soon as the page is displayed,
  even if it is at the bottom.
{% endcomment %}
{% if texts %}
<div class="error-zone" role="alert">
  {% for text in texts %}
  <div>{{ text }}</div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}

The two inclusion tag templates [success_zone] and [error_zone] (web layer, above): they receive the list [texts], prepared by the tag, and display it. [role="status"]: A screen reader announces the success message. [role="alert"]: It announces the error section as soon as the page is displayed, even if it is at the bottom. The error section remains anchored at the bottom of the window when the page is long (see the stylesheet below).

docs.title: 11.18.1.4. templates/fragments/confirmation.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/confirmation.html - the "Are you sure?" modal dialog
  (see example 21).

  It replaces the window.confirm() box of the browser, which can neither be
  styled nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the browser, not
  in that of the page).

  A SINGLE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its labels
  are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page; the small script
  static/js/app.js merely displays it, puts in it the message specific to the
  form (data-confirmation attribute), and sends the form if
  the user confirms.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">{% translate "Confirmation" %}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="{% translate 'Close' %}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes "Cancel this appointment?" #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">{% translate "No, go back" %}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">{% translate "Yes, confirm" %}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The “Are you sure?” modal window from Example 21, which replaces the browser’s [window.confirm()] dialog box: this dialog box does not format correctly, and its buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s language. A single window for the entire page, initially hidden (class [d-none] derived from [Bootstrap]); its labels are translated by the server, just like the rest of the page. The [static/js/app.js] script displays it, places the message from the form to be confirmed inside it (its [data-confirmation] attribute), and submits the form if the user confirms. The "Cancel" button is labeled “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context. The attributes [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal], [aria-labelledby], and [aria-describedby] describe the window to screen readers: a dialog box awaiting a response, its title, and its message.

docs.title: 11.18.1.5. templates/fragments/booking.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/booking.html - the booking dialog of the schedule.

  The REAL Bootstrap classes of a modal dialog (.modal, .modal-backdrop...),
  made visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than by the JavaScript of
  Bootstrap. It is the SERVER that decides to display it (&book=... parameter of
  the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link to the same page without this
  parameter.

  The fragment directly reads the variables of the page that includes it
  (booking, doctor_id, day, back_url).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'schedule_book' %}" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">{% translate "Book this slot" %}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ back_url }}" aria-label="{% translate 'Close' %}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{% blocktranslate with time_range=booking.time_range %}Slot {{ time_range }}{% endblocktranslate %}</p>

        {# what the server must know in addition to the chosen patient #}
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ doctor_id }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ day }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="{{ booking.slot_id }}">

        {# a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from (and the server ignores any clientId anyway) #}
        {% if booking.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{% translate "Patient" %}</span>:
          <strong>{{ booking.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="clientId">{% translate "Patient" %}</label>
        <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choose a patient --" %}</option>
          {% for client in booking.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ back_url }}">{% translate "Cancel" %}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Confirm" %}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

The calendar booking window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), but made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]), rather than via the [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap]: it is the server that decides to display it when URL contains [&book=...]. Closing it (using the X or the Cancel button) is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([back_url]).

  • Line 26: [{% blocktranslate with time_range=booking.time_range %}]: a translated text that contains a variable (example 22). In a [blocktranslate], only simple variables are allowed ([{{ time_range }}], not [{{ booking.time_range }}]): the [with] clause creates one;
  • lines 29–32: the anti-CSRF token, and what the server needs to know: the doctor, the day, and the time slot;
  • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name, with no list to choose from (and the server ignores any [clientId] field anyway). The administrator and doctors select the patient from a list; [required] and [autofocus]: the browser requires a selection and places the cursor in the list.

docs.title: 11.18.1.6. templates/fragments/captcha.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/captcha.html - the captcha of the authentication page
  (see security/captchas.py). It protects both login and access to the
  account creation (button "Create a patient account"). It reads the variable
  [captcha] of the page.

  captcha.svg|safe: the SVG image is inserted AS IS in the page, without
  escaping. It is safe here because this SVG is made by the server
  itself and contains nothing that comes from the user - one would NEVER do
  that with user input.

  The hidden field captcha_id tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
  answer, for its part, is never sent to the browser. "Another image" simply reloads
  the page ({% url 'login' %}: the URL of the page, without its parameters).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{% translate "Type the characters shown in the image" %}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{% translate 'Anti-robot verification image' %}">{{ captcha.svg|safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Another image" %}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captcha_id" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{% translate "Upper or lower case, it does not matter." %}</div>
</div>

The CAPTCHA (example 27). [captcha.svg|safe] inserts the image SVG as-is, without escaping it: otherwise, the browser would display its code XML. This is safe here because this SVG is generated by the server and contains nothing provided by the user: we would never do this with user input. The hidden field [captcha_id] tells the server which CAPTCHA to verify; the response itself is never sent to the browser. The “Another image” link reloads the login page—and thus the CAPTCHA. The attributes of the input fields ([autocomplete="off"], [autocapitalize="off"], [spellcheck="false"]) prevent the browser from suggesting a previous entry and the phone’s keyboard from capitalizing letters or correcting spelling.

docs.title: 11.18.2.1. templates/forms/field.html
docs.text:
{% comment %}
  templates/forms/field.html - a complete field of a form: label,
  input zone, then its error message or its help (see example 18 and the
  FORM_RENDERER setting). The input zone is framed in red (class
  is-invalid) by the flag method of the form (see web/forms.py).
{% endcomment %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
  {{ field }}
  {% if field.errors %}<div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_error">{% for error in field.errors %}{{ error }}{% if not forloop.last %}<br>{% endif %}{% endfor %}</div>{% endif %}
  {% if field.help_text and not field.errors %}<div class="form-text" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_helptext">{{ field.help_text }}</div>{% endif %}
</div>

The template for a complete field—that of the [BootstrapRenderer] rendering engine (web layer, above)—as shown in Example 18: the label, the input field ([{{ field }}], with the classes CSS provided by the form), followed by the error message or, if none, the help text. The classes [invalid-feedback] (the message in red) and [form-text] (the help text in gray) are those of [Bootstrap]; [d-block] displays the message even if the input field is not immediately preceding it. A field may have multiple errors: they are separated by a line break ([forloop.last], example 14).

The identifiers [..._error] and [..._helptext] are not chosen at random: these are the ones that [Django] refers to in the [aria-describedby] attributes of the input field, with [aria-invalid] for a field with an error. A screen reader thus reads the error message or help text along with the field:

<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="id_first_name">First name</label>
  <input type="text" name="first_name" maxlength="20" class="form-control is-invalid" required aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="id_first_name_error" id="id_first_name">
  <div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="id_first_name_error">The first name is required.</div>
</div>

The red border ([is-invalid]) was added by the form’s [flag] method; [maxlength] and [required] by [Django], based on the field’s options. The [required] attribute does not prevent an empty form from being submitted: the application’s forms carry the [novalidate] attribute (see below); validation is performed by the server.

{% endcomment %}

    <div class="col-sm-6">{{ form.first_name.as_field_group }}</div>
